mcqs.question: In the modern periodic table, which of the following correctly defines a period and a group?

options.A: A period is a horizontal row; a group is a vertical column of elements having similar chemical properties.
options.B: A period is a vertical column; a group is a horizontal row of elements having similar atomic masses.
options.C: A period is a diagonal line; a group is a set of elements with the same number of neutrons.
options.D: A period is a set of elements with the same valence electrons; a group is a set of elements with the same atomic number.

mcqs.answer: A period is a horizontal row; a group is a vertical column of elements having similar chemical properties.
mcqs.explanation: A period runs horizontally across the table and indicates the number of electron shells; a group runs vertically and contains elements with similar chemical behaviour because they have the same valence‑electron configuration. Options B, C and D give incorrect definitions.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand blocks of the periodic table
mcqs.question: The element with electron configuration [Ar] 4s² 3d¹⁰ 4p² belongs to which block of the periodic table?
mcqs.explanation: The outermost electrons are in the 4p subshell, which places the element in the p‑block. s‑block elements end in ns¹ or ns², d‑block elements end in (n‑1)d, and f‑block elements involve (n‑2)f electrons. Hence only option B is correct.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate electronic configuration to periodic position
mcqs.question: An element has the electron configuration [Ne] 3s² 3p⁵. In which period and group does it appear?
mcqs.explanation: The highest principal quantum number is n=3, so the element is in period 3. The valence configuration ends with p⁵, characteristic of the halogens, which occupy group 17. Therefore option B is correct; the other options mismatch either period or group.

mcqs.question: A new element X is discovered with atomic number 119. According to the modern periodic law, which statement is true about its placement?

options.A: It will be placed in period 8 and will have properties similar to alkali metals.
options.B: It will be placed in period 7 and will be a noble gas.
options.C: It will be placed in period 8 and will be a transition metal.
options.D: It will be placed in period 7 and will be a halogen.

mcqs.answer: It will be placed in period 8 and will have properties similar to alkali metals.
mcqs.explanation: The modern periodic law states that elements are arranged by increasing atomic number. An element with Z = 119 starts a new period (period 8) and, being the first element of that period, belongs to group 1, the alkali‑metal group. Options B, C and D place the element in the wrong period or group.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly reflects the basis of the modern periodic table?

options.A: Elements are arranged in order of increasing atomic mass.
options.B: Elements are arranged in order of increasing atomic number.
options.C: Elements are arranged according to similar chemical properties only, ignoring atomic number.

mcqs.answer: Elements are arranged in order of increasing atomic number.
mcqs.explanation: Mendeleev’s original table used atomic mass, but the modern periodic table is ordered by atomic number (Z). This ordering resolves earlier anomalies. Options A, C and D are incorrect representations of the modern arrangement.

mcqs.question: If element Y is located in the 4th period and 2nd group of the periodic table, which of the following statements must be true?

options.A: It has four electron shells and its outermost electron configuration ends with s².
options.B: It has two electron shells and its outermost electron configuration ends with p².
options.D: It belongs to the lanthanide series.

mcqs.answer: It has four electron shells and its outermost electron configuration ends with s².
mcqs.explanation: Period 4 indicates n=4 electron shells. Group 2 elements have an ns² valence configuration (s‑block). Therefore statement A is necessarily true. Options B, C and D contradict the given period/group information.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand blocks of the periodic table
mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly compares s‑block and p‑block elements?

options.A: s‑block elements have valence electrons only in an ns¹ or ns² configuration, whereas p‑block elements have valence electrons in both ns² and np¹‑⁶ configurations.
options.B: s‑block elements have valence electrons in d orbitals, while p‑block elements have valence electrons in f orbitals.
options.C: s‑block elements are non‑metals and p‑block elements are metals.
options.D: s‑block elements are located on the right side of the table and p‑block elements on the left side.

mcqs.answer: s‑block elements have valence electrons only in an ns¹ or ns² configuration, whereas p‑block elements have valence electrons in both ns² and np¹‑⁶ configurations.
mcqs.explanation: s‑block comprises groups 1 and 2 with configurations ns¹ or ns². p‑block (groups 13‑18) has a filled ns² core plus np electrons (1 to 6). Options B, C and D describe incorrect orbital or positional characteristics.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate electronic configuration to periodic position
mcqs.question: The element with configuration [Kr] 5s² 4d¹⁰ 5p³ is located in which period and group?
mcqs.explanation: The highest principal quantum number is n=5, placing the element in period 5. The valence electrons are ns² np³, characteristic of group 15 (pnictogens). Option B matches both period and group; the other options either give the wrong group or shift the period to 6.
